courses.title: Learn Vue 3: Step by Step
courses.description:
Go from your very first Vue template to components, composables and state management with Pinia.

Vue is one of the most approachable JavaScript frameworks, and Vue 3 makes it even more powerful. In this series we start with nothing more than a script tag and build up, one idea at a time, to a real application structure.

Each episode is short and focused. We pause to discuss the mistakes beginners usually make, and the "little confusing things" that rarely get explained, so you understand why Vue behaves the way it does.

By the end you will be comfortable building components, sharing state between them, and organising a Vue project with modern tooling.

## What you'll learn

• Create reactive Vue 3 applications and bind data, attributes and events
• Render lists and conditionals, and use computed properties
• Build reusable components and pass data with props and events
• Handle forms with v-model and communicate between parent and child components
• Use slots to create flexible components
• Set up a project with Vite and the script setup syntax
• Extract logic into composables and share data with provide/inject
• Manage application state with Pinia

## Requirements

• Basic HTML, CSS and JavaScript
• A code editor and a modern browser
• Node.js installed for the later episodes

## Who this course is for

• Beginners who know some JavaScript and want to learn Vue
• Developers moving from jQuery or other frameworks
• Laravel developers who want a modern front end

## Course details

**Instructor:** Laracasts
**Video source:** YouTube playlist "Learn Vue 3: Step By Step" by Laracasts
**Video language:** English, can be dubbed into many languages
**Content:** 27 lessons · about 4.7 hours

lessons.title: The Absolute Basics
lessons.description: Let's start...at the beginning! We'll pull in Vue 3 through a CDN, and then review the absolute basics of the framework, including Vue initialization, text interpolation, and reactivity.

lessons.title: Attribute Binding and Event Handling
lessons.description: You'll often want to bind the value of an HTML attribute to an expression. We can allow for this by using the v-bind directive. As part of this lesson, we'll also get a first taste of event handling in Vue.

lessons.title: Lists, Conditionals, and Computed Properties
lessons.description: Let's dig into a few more important concepts in this episode. Using the example of an assignment list, we'll learn how to loop over arrays, conditionally display HTML, and prepare computed properties.

lessons.title: Your First Vue Component
lessons.description: We've now learned the absolute basics of Vue; however, this still looks nothing like real-life Vue applications. Let's begin digging into custom Vue components.

lessons.title: One Vue Component Per File
lessons.description: We can technically inline child Vue components, but you'll rarely do so. Instead, a much cleaner approach is to store each Vue component within its own file. Let's take care of that in this episode.

lessons.title: Component Props
lessons.description: If we want our Vue components to be as flexible as possible, we should figure out a way to pass in data from the outside. This way, each "instance" of a component can be configurable. Props allow for this!

lessons.title: Bring it All Together
lessons.description: Let's now return to the simple assignment lists that we worked on in episode three. But this time, we'll approach it with fresh eyes and a new understanding of how Vue components work.

lessons.title: Handle a Form Submission
lessons.description: In this episode, we'll combine forms and events to allow a user to create new assignments on the fly.

lessons.title: Parent-Child State Communication
lessons.description: Now, let's throw a wrench into the mix. If we extract a new Vue component, we'll then need to figure out how our components should communicate state changes.

lessons.title: It's All So Easy
lessons.description: Once you understand the basics of Vue, you'll quickly find that things, which were incredibly time consuming years ago, can now be accomplished in seconds. Let's review a couple examples in this video.

lessons.title: Component Responsibility
lessons.description: In this episode, we'll discuss component responsibility as we refactor to an AssignmentsTags component. I think of component responsibility in the same way that I think of server-side class responsibility. "Does this bit of logic belong here?"

lessons.title: A Deeper Look at v-model
lessons.description: We reviewed the basics of the v-model directive at the beginning of the series, but I think it's time that we take a deeper look. What exactly happens when we apply v-model to an input? And can we also use it on custom Vue components?

lessons.title: Lifecycle Hooks, Fake APIs, and AJAX
lessons.description: So far, we've been hard-coding the list of assignments directly within our Vue component. But of course, that's not overly realistic. Let's switch over to using the fetch() JavaScript API to request data from a fake API.

lessons.title: Flexible Vue Components With Slots and Flags
lessons.description: There are many ways to allow for more flexible and configurable components. Let's begin with two simple and obvious techniques: slots and flags.

lessons.title: Named Slots
lessons.description: So far, we've been working with components that only required a single, default slot. But, of course in real life, you'll encounter situations where you need to insert content in multiple areas. In these cases, we can used named slots.

lessons.title: An Introduction to Vite
lessons.description: Great job, if you've made it this far. I think you're now ready to move on to part two of this series. Now that you understand many of the fundamentals of Vue, let's now figure out how to actually construct a single-page application using it.

lessons.title: Little Confusing Things About Vue
lessons.description: At this stage, I fully expect you to be confused in numerous ways. We went from building basic Vue components to scaffolding a full single-page application with routing, configuration, aliases, and more.

lessons.title: Two Mental Leaps to Script Setup
lessons.description: I must admit, I feel bad for what I'm about to do. You were becoming so comfortable, and I had to suddenly throw a wrench into the gears. In this lesson, let's mentally adjust to working with the Composition API and script setup.

lessons.title: From Mixins to Composables
lessons.description: Let's talk about code re-use in this episode. We'll begin by reviewing a basic example using a traditional, mixin-based approach. And then, we'll convert it to the more recommended approach these days: composables.

lessons.title: Composables Example
lessons.description: Let's review another example of a composable. This time, we'll leverage localStorage and Vue reactivity to "remember" a form input's value - even if you refresh the page.

courses.title: Angular Tutorial for Beginners
courses.description:
Learn Angular from the ground up, from components and data binding to services, routing and forms.

Angular is a complete platform for building large, maintainable web applications. This course introduces the framework one concept at a time, with a small, runnable example in every lesson.

You will start with components and templates, move on to directives, services and HTTP, and finish with two complete series on template-driven and reactive forms.

The lessons are short, so you can follow the whole path or jump straight to the topic you need.

## What you'll learn

• Create an Angular project and understand its structure
• Build components and use interpolation, property, class, style and event binding
• Control templates with ngIf, ngSwitch and ngFor
• Share data between components and format output with pipes
• Use services and dependency injection
• Fetch data over HTTP with observables and handle errors
• Configure routing, route parameters and child routes
• Build and validate template-driven and reactive forms

• Basic HTML, CSS and JavaScript
• Some familiarity with TypeScript is helpful
• Node.js and a code editor installed

Laravel is one of the most loved PHP frameworks, with an elegant syntax and everything you need to build modern web applications. In this series we build one up step by step, starting with routes and views.

Build a complete full-stack CRUD application with MongoDB, Express, React and Node.js, and deploy it.

The MERN stack lets you build an entire web application in JavaScript. In this series we build a user-management app from an empty folder to a deployed project.

First we create the REST API with Express and MongoDB, then a React front end with routing and forms, and finally we connect the two and ship the result.

courses.description:
A university-style foundation course on how people communicate, from perception and listening to persuasion and media.

Good communication is the skill that makes every other skill work. This course follows the structure of a college introduction to human communication, explaining why we misunderstand each other and what research says about doing it better.

Each lesson is short and example-driven. You will look at identity, culture, language, listening and nonverbal cues, then apply the ideas to relationships, the workplace and the media you use every day.

## What you'll learn

• Define communication and what makes someone a competent communicator
• Understand how identity, culture and perception shape messages
• Recognise your conflict style and handle disagreements constructively
• Listen actively and read nonverbal cues
• Build and maintain healthy personal and professional relationships
• Apply the principles of persuasion and spot common influence tactics

## Requirements

• No prior knowledge needed
• Curiosity about how people interact
• Optional: a notebook to reflect on your own communication habits

## Who this course is for

• Students starting a communication or business degree
• Professionals who want to communicate more effectively
• Anyone who wants to improve their relationships

## Course details

**Instructor:** Study Hall
**Video source:** YouTube playlist "Intro to Human Communication: College Foundations" by Study Hall 
**Video language:** English, can be dubbed into many languages
**Content:** 30 lessons · about 5.2 hours

lessons.title: Preview: Intro to Human Communication
lessons.description: Communication is a tool that is ingrained in our daily interactions, but have you ever wondered how it works and why it's important? Communication might be more complex than we realize as it can adapt and change depending on a wide array of factors.

lessons.title: Introduction and Definition of Communication
lessons.description: You cannot escape communication! No matter what we're doing, we're always communicating. Whether through verbal or non-verbal cues, communication is how we interact with our surroundings. In this episode, we discuss meaning-making, and what communication really means.

lessons.title: Working Toward Competent Communication
lessons.description: Whether it be in professional settings or when communicating with authority figures, there's the expectation that each party can communicate competently. Regardless of the setting, being able to get messages across effectively is an important skill.

lessons.title: Identity and Culture in Communication
lessons.description: We often tend to ignore what we consider normal, and pay attention when something unusual happens. Two factors of communication that function this way are identity and culture.

lessons.title: Perception
lessons.description: How does our perception affect our communication? What we take in with our senses and how our brains interpret that information doesn’t always match up because there’s often too much going on for our brains to process every single detail accurately!

lessons.title: Cross Cultural Communication Challenges
lessons.description: When communicating across cultures, it is easy to lean into aspects that are easily visible like food, dress and important celebrations; but there's many more cultural elements that hide under the surface.

lessons.title: How Power Affects Communication
lessons.description: Our perception of who has power and why they do is shaped by the values of the cultures and societies we live in. These trickle down into our communities, families and workplaces, and affect our behavior and how we interact with other people.

lessons.title: Being Direct or Getting Emotional
lessons.description: When we read between the lines, we're looking beyond literal interpretations to implications from verbal cues. While some people say exactly what they mean, leaving little room for interpretation, others make statements that imply the emotional truth behind a message.

lessons.title: What Is Your Conflict Style?
lessons.description: People handle conflict differently depending on the context and situation they find themselves in. In this episode, we discuss conflict and conflict styles in different contexts so that we can better handle situations when they arise.

lessons.title: How is Language Built?
lessons.description: The way we choose and use words, whether it be speaking, writing, or signing, is shaped by language. Language is a system we use to express ideas by combining sounds, gestures, and symbols into words, phrases, and sentences.

lessons.title: How Verbal Communication affects Perception
lessons.description: The words we use serve to describe everything from the tangible to the abstract, what we know to what we can't quite describe. And the words that make up our language actually shape the way in which we think and perceive the world around us.

lessons.title: Listening
lessons.description: Listening constitutes half or more of everything we communicate. Through listening we are able to understand context and find the right strategies to share our messages in every type of setting. In this episode, we discuss listening and the ways in which this process makes for richer communication.

lessons.title: Nonverbal Communication
lessons.description: We are communicating all of the time, whether we speak or not. Through our body language and mannerisms, we constantly put our emotions and thoughts out into the world.

lessons.title: Nonverbal Cues and the Use of Space, Touch, and Time
lessons.description: A lot of things impact how we make meaning, from how close we stand to each other to how we incorporate touch into our conversations. In this episode, we discuss nonverbal cues and how the use of space, touch and time shape meaning and context in different cultures.

lessons.title: Creating and maintaining strong, healthy relationships
lessons.description: Ever wondered why you're attracted to some people and not others? In human relationships and interactions, attraction is so much more than just people being drawn together. But, with the power of communication and attraction theory, we can explain the forces that draw us together.

lessons.title: Social Penetration Theory (Ogres Are Like Onions)
lessons.description: When building relationships, sharing deeply personal information can make us feel vulnerable. Understanding certain patterns can help us identify how much information to share at different stages so that we are able to get to know others while still protecting our privacy.

lessons.title: Creating Bonds: Knapp’s Relationship Development Model
lessons.description: Like a lot of things in life, our relationships go through stages. Recognizing these stages helps us understand and communicate about our own relationships better.

lessons.title: Relational Dialectics
lessons.description: Life is full of competing desires, like wanting to know what you're getting for your birthday but also wanting to be surprised. These opposing wants may at times create strains in our relationships if we don't exercise intentional communication.

lessons.title: Creating Healthy Relationships
lessons.description: How we communicate affects how our relationships develop, having the power to deepen or break the bonds we create. Being aware of what communication styles and behaviors can impact bonds negatively can help us be more aware when building successful relationships.

lessons.title: The Importance of Communication in the Workplace
lessons.description: If there's something that most, if not all, professions have in common, is the need to communicate effectively. From having respectful interactions with customers to making persuasive recommendations during a pitch, being able to successfully convey a message is necessary.

lessons.title: Organizational Structure
lessons.description: When working within an organization, we are aware of the expectations for how people in different positions communicate with one another. The way in which you address your co-worker in the same position as you and your CEO might look different.

lessons.title: Impression Management and Self-Monitoring
lessons.description: Every gathering of people or organization is going to either clearly or subtly shape what’s expected, as far as conversation topics, attitudes, and behaviors go. So many factors impact what is considered “appropriate” for a context.

lessons.title: Business Apologies: How to spot the fakes
lessons.description: From messed up orders to lost luggage, there might be times when organizations make mistakes. That’s because organizations are made up of people–and people make mistakes because no one is perfect.

lessons.title: Introducing Persuasion
lessons.description: Persuasion is hiding all around us. From design choices to the way we speak, all of these things are part of efforts to communicate information that could influence our choices.

lessons.title: Learning the Principles of Persuasion
lessons.description: Between instincts and forming associations, a lot of our behavior is automatic, made up of a combination of instincts and learned associations. Which means many of our decisions and actions are influenced by environmental and social cues, often in ways we aren’t conscious of.

lessons.title: The Ways We Can Be Swayed
lessons.description: When we use the principles of persuasion in ethical ways by being truthful, authentic, and respectful, we can share our viewpoints with others to build consensus. And we can use these principles in many types of communication…like verbal, nonverbal, and organizational communication.

lessons.title: History of Mass Media

lessons.title: How to Clear a Backlog - The 4 Rs Method

lessons.title: How to manage relationships

lessons.title: How to set Boundaries and practice Assertiveness

lessons.title: Relationship Management and Communication

courses.title: Leadership at Work
courses.description:
A complete tour of leadership theory and practice, from styles and situational models to leading teams and developing leaders.

Leadership is learned. This course explains the major models, from traits and behaviours to transformational, servant and situational leadership, and shows how to use them in daily management.

It then turns to leading teams and developing other leaders through mentoring and coaching, and closes with the ideas of leading thinkers such as Bennis, Kouzes and Posner and Simon Sinek.

## What you'll learn

• Describe the leadership skill set and the 10-step leadership process
• Compare trait, behavioural and style-based models
• Recognise transactional, transformational, servant and authentic leadership
• Apply situational and contingency leadership models
• Lead teams using Tuckman, Adair and the team leadership continuum
• Develop leaders through mentoring and coaching

## Requirements

• No prior knowledge
• Some experience leading people helps but is not required
• Openness to reflect on your own style

## Who this course is for

• New and aspiring managers
• Team leaders who want a framework
• Students of management and business

## Course details

**Instructor:** Mike Clayton
**Video source:** YouTube playlist "Leadership at Work: Essential Skills for Modern Managers" by Management Courses - Mike Clayton
**Video language:** English, can be dubbed into many languages
**Content:** 36 lessons · about 5.0 hours

lessons.title: What is Leadership? and Why do We Need Leaders?
lessons.description: In this video, I answer two questions, to kick off our series on Leadership: what is leadership, and why do we need it?

lessons.title: The Leadership Skill Set: What Every Leader Needs to be Able to Do
lessons.description: In this video, I look at the leadership skills a leader needs to acquire in a workplace setting. It’s a long list, so buckle up.

lessons.title: Leadership Attitudes: How to Approach Things Like a Leader
lessons.description: Leadership is largely a matter of character. Yes, there are some skills you’ll need, some roles to discharge, and a choice of how you do it. But, first and foremost, what matters are your attitudes to leadership and the people you lead.

lessons.title: 10-Step Leadership Process: A Simple Model for How to Lead
lessons.description: In this video, I offer you a ten-step Leadership Process. Watching this video is worth 2 Management Courses CPD Points*.

lessons.title: What is Leader-Member Exchange Theory? And Should You Use LMX Theory?
lessons.description: Leader-Member Exchange Theory is deeply problematic. In fact, I don’t like it. But it may be a model you want to adopt. It is certainly a theory you need to understand, so you can avoid its Dark Side.

lessons.title: Traits Models of Leadership
lessons.description: There are many approaches to modeling leadership. But, perhaps the oldest assumes that leaders are people born with a specific set of qualities, or traits. Today, we still recognize that there are some traits that can make us better leaders. If only we could agree on which!

lessons.title: Leadership Behaviors: Task and Relationship Focus
lessons.description: In the middle of the 20th Century, researchers turned their attention from how leaders are, to what to what they do. With a suitable behavioral theory of leadership, we can more easily train leaders. They found the key concepts are task and relationship.

lessons.title: Action Centered Leadership - A Roles-based or Functional Leadership Model
lessons.description: Roles-based approaches to leadership focus not on the leader’s traits nor their behavior. Instead, they focus on their functions: what they need to do, to lead. And none is better, nor more accessible, than John Adair’s Action Centered Leadership model.

lessons.title: Goleman's 6 Leadership Styles - A Styles Models of Leadership
lessons.description: We’ve seen models of leadership based on personal traits, individual behaviors, and the roles we need to fulfill. Another approach relates to the way we lead: that is, the style we adopt.

lessons.title: What is Transactional Leadership?
lessons.description: Watching this video is worth 1 Management Courses CPD Point*. Program 3: Managing and Leading Individuals

lessons.title: What is Transformational Leadership?
lessons.description: Transformational leadership is a story in three parts. But those parts are closely integrated, so buckle up for a longer video than usual.

lessons.title: The Blake & Mouton Leadership Grid
lessons.description: Robert Blake and Jane Mouton took the idea of task versus relationship focus and turned it into a full-blown model of five leadership styles: their Leadership Grid.

lessons.title: What is Visionary Leadership?
lessons.description: Visionary leadership is transformative. We could argue that it is one aspect of transformational leadership. But I want to consider it as a specific style, because we find many leaders who seem aim for this style as their default.

lessons.title: What is Charismatic Leadership?
lessons.description: Charismatic leadership combines charm, interpersonal skills, and persuasiveness to motivate and influence others.

lessons.title: What is Authentic Leadership?
lessons.description: Authentic leadership is still a relatively new and under-researched topic. It first came to wide attention with the 2006 best seller, ‘Why Should Anyone be Led by You’, by British academics, Rob Goffee and Gareth Jones. But it goes back way further than that.

lessons.title: What is Servant Leadership?
lessons.description: Servant Leadership is one of my favorite concepts. For me it’s a no brainer. So, let me explain why.

lessons.title: Fiedler's Contingency Model REMAINS Highly Relevant TODAY
lessons.description: Fred Fiedler developed a contingency model of leadership that suggests a leader’s effectiveness is contingent on the fit between their leadership style and the situation they face. This video explores the Fiedler Contingency Theory of Leadership Effectiveness.

lessons.title: Tannenbaum & Schmidt: The Leadership Continuum
lessons.description: Tannenbaum and Schmidt’s Leadership Continuum is a situational leadership model, offering a range of styles and ways to select among them.

lessons.title: Situational Leadership: A Generic Day-to-Day Model
lessons.description: In this video, I will explain the basics of situational leadership, using generic terminology.

lessons.title: Commercial Situational Leadership Models
lessons.description: In the last video, I described a basic generic model of Situational Leadership. There are two detailed commercial Situational Leadership models on the market:

lessons.title: Robert House and Path Goal Theory [Situational Leadership]
lessons.description: Path-Goal Theory is a contingency model of leadership. Like other situational leadership models, the approach you take to leading is dependent on the situation. In this case, you look at the people you are leading and the nature of the task.

lessons.title: Complexity, Leadership, and the Cynefin Framework
lessons.description: The Cynefin Framework is a description of the nature of different situations. And each situation merits a different kind of leadership.

lessons.title: Team Leadership and the Tuckman Group Development Stages
lessons.description: In an earlier video, we looked at the Tuckman Model of Group Development. Now, we'll tie the different stages to the style of team leadership that will work best in each stage.

lessons.title: Servant Leadership: Leading Your Team in the Tuckman Performing Stage
lessons.description: Watching this video is worth 2 Management Courses CPD Points*. This video is part of course module number 4.3.3

lessons.title: Team Leadership: What is John Adair's Action Centered Leadership?
lessons.description: John Adair's Action Centered Leadership model (sometimes known as the three circles model) is one of the best models for Team Leadership. Every manager should know it.

lessons.title: LEAD Your Team: 4 Team Leadership Priorities
lessons.description: Here is a very simple model of four team leadership priorities - which spell out LEAD. Can you guess what they are?

lessons.title: Four Quadrants of Team Leadership
lessons.description: A team can focus on two things: task and relationship. And, for each, there are 2 elements: the content and the process. This gives us 4 quadrants of team leadership.

lessons.title: What is the Team Leadership Continuum? [Tannenbaum & Schmidt]
lessons.description: Robert Tannenbaum and Warren H Schmidt set out a range of leadership behaviours. This model gives us a powerful team leadership continuum.

lessons.title: Daniel Goleman's 6 Leadership Styles for Team Leaders
lessons.description: In his book, The New Leaders, Daniel Goleman and his co-authors set out 6 leadership styles for team leaders.

lessons.title: Team Leadership: Handling Team Problems
lessons.description: Team working is not always smooth and easy. So, an essential part of team leadership is handling team problems. Here we look at the basics of how to handle 8 common team problems.

lessons.title: The Principles of Leadership Development
lessons.description: Leaders are not born to lead. They acquire leadership skills through experience and learning. I want to look at some of the principles of leadership development.

lessons.title: Mentoring for Leadership Development
lessons.description: This video is part of course module number 3.11.4 Program 3: Managing and Leading Individuals

lessons.title: Coaching for Leadership Development
lessons.description: The best leaders have been coaching and being coached for years. But, in the modern business world, we have systems, processes, and frameworks to help us. At its best, coaching is a conversation that helps one person figure out what they need to do to get the results they want.

lessons.title: Warren Bennis: Master of Transformative Leadership
lessons.description: Warren Bennis is not just an expert on leadership – which he undoubtedly is. He created the modern interest in the subject, with the book he co-wrote with Burt Nanus: ‘Leaders: The Strategies for Taking Charge’.

lessons.title: Kouzes and Posner: The Leadership Challenge
lessons.description: If you want to make extraordinary things happen, you are going to face challenges. That’s the thesis of James Kouzes and Barry Posner.

lessons.title: Simon Sinek: Start with Why and Leaders Eat Last
lessons.description: Simon Sinek is an American author and speaker. Two of his books have had a huge influence on leaders in business and public service: Start with Why, and Leaders Eat Last.

courses.title: Project Management for Beginners
courses.description:
Learn the core ideas, tools and vocabulary of project management in short, clear lessons.

This beginner course explains what a project is, what a project manager does and how a project moves from definition to delivery.

You will meet the key tools, including scope, the iron triangle, milestones, Gantt charts, work breakdown structures, critical path and risk management, plus an introduction to Agile.

## What you'll learn

• Explain what project management is and the role of the project manager
• Define a project with scope, a business case and the iron triangle
• Plan with milestones, Gantt charts, WBS and the critical path
• Manage stakeholders and project risk
• Understand the basics of Agile project management
• Avoid scope creep and write simple progress reports

## Requirements

• No prior knowledge
• No special software
• A small project to apply the ideas to

## Who this course is for

• People about to manage their first project
• Team members who work with project managers
• Anyone considering a project-management career

**Video source:** YouTube playlist "Project Management Beginners" by Online PM Courses - Mike Clayton

lessons.title: Project Management 101: Beginner's Guide to Project Management
lessons.description: Welcome to our Beginner's Guide to Project Management. This Project Management 101 is not for dummies, nor for idiots. Because that's not who you are. But there's no shame in being a beginner: we all started at the beginning!

lessons.title: Project Management Fundamentals: 40 minute Outline of the Project Management Process
lessons.description: Project Management Fundamentals is a short project management course that will introduce you to the absolute essentials of the four stages of Project Management.

lessons.description: Here's our list of the top 12 project management jargon terms. We've based this list on the most viewed videos in our Project Management in Under 5 Minutes series:

lessons.title: What is a Project Definition? Project Management in Under 5
lessons.description: The first stage of a formal project methodology is Project Definition. So, what is a Project Definition?

lessons.description: What is the Project Manager's Iron Triangle? It is also known as the Time-Cost-Quality Triangle, The Triple Constraint, and The Triangle of Balance.

lessons.title: What is Stakeholder Management? Project Management in Under 5

lessons.title: Project Planning 101 - How to Build Effective Project Plans

lessons.description: What is Project Risk Management? Project Managers know that projects are risky. Risk management is therefore a vital discipline. Indeed, a focus on project risk is a sign of real project management maturity.

lessons.title: Project Risk Management - How to Manage Project Risk
lessons.description: When you are managing a project, risk is always with you. So, Project Risk Management is a fundamental discipline.

lessons.title: What is Agile Project Management? Project Management in Under 5

lessons.description: Are you considering a Project Management career? And are you wondering, ‘Is Project Management a good career choice?’ Come to think of it, you’re probably also wondering if it pays well!

courses.title: Negotiation Skills at Work
courses.description:
Prepare, open, bargain and close negotiations, and learn the tools used by master negotiators.

Negotiation is a skill every professional uses daily. This course teaches a complete process, from preparation to follow-up, with the key concepts behind it.

You will study strategies, behaviours, power and leverage, practise tools such as questioning, listening and empathic negotiation, and learn from classic books by Fisher, Voss and others.

## What you'll learn

• Follow the stages of a negotiation from preparation to closing
• Choose between the five basic negotiating strategies
• Understand power, leverage and the scope for agreement
• Handle difficult behaviour, deadlock and breakdown
• Ask questions, listen and use empathy as negotiating tools
• Apply ideas from Getting to Yes and Never Split the Difference

## Requirements

• No prior knowledge
• Some experience of workplace discussions is helpful
• A real negotiation to prepare, for practice

## Who this course is for

• Managers and team leaders
• Sales, procurement and account professionals

lessons.title: Fundamental Model of Negotiation - the Basic Negotiation Process
lessons.description: Some people find the idea of negotiating uncomfortable. It feels like negotiation is about asking for more than you deserve. It is not. In this video, we'll get started on the basics with the Fundamental Model of Negotiation.

lessons.description: A large part of the success of your negotiation will come from the preparation stage. This is where you think about the outcome you want from your negotiation.

lessons.title: Opening Stage of the Negotiation Process
lessons.description: The opening stage of a negotiation is where the parties first come together. It sets up a shared basis for the negotiation to come.

lessons.title: Bargaining Stage of the Negotiation Process

lessons.title: Negotiating Team Roles in the Negotiation Process
lessons.description: Watching this video is worth 1 Management Courses CPD Point*. This video is part of course module number 5.2.1

lessons.title: Closing Stage of the Negotiation Process

lessons.title: Negotiation Follow-up - after the Negotiating Process
lessons.description: Watching this video is worth 1 Management Courses CPD Point*. This video is part of course module number 5.2.1

lessons.title: Five Basic Negotiating Strategies
lessons.description: What is your strategy when you go into a negotiation? There are five basic negotiating strategies. In this video, I'll describe them, based on the work of Kenneth Thomas and Ralph Kilmann.

lessons.title: Scope for Agreement

lessons.title: The Psychology of YES: How to Get Agreement with Mike’s Slicing the Pie Method

lessons.title: Four Primary Negotiating Behaviors
lessons.description: Watching this video is worth 1 Management Courses CPD Point*. This video is part of course module number 5.2.2

lessons.title: Power at the Negotiating Table: Key Concepts in Negotiation
lessons.description: Everybody goes into a negotiation with power. The power to say yes, to say no, to move the negotiation forwards, or to frustrate progress. But where does this power come from?

lessons.title: Negotiation Goes Bad: How to Handle 6 Types of Bad Behavior

lessons.title: Listening Skills

lessons.title: What is Empathic Negotiation?

lessons.title: Influencing and Persuading

lessons.title: How to Handle a Negotiation Breakdown

courses.title: Python Programming for Beginners
courses.description:
A clear, practical introduction to Python, from strings and loops to modules, files and testing.

Corey Schafer’s Python series is known for clear explanations and real examples. It starts with installing Python and the core data types, then moves to functions, modules and the standard library.

Later lessons cover files, CSV, dates, sorting, error handling, unit testing, virtual environments and web requests, the skills you need for real scripts.

## What you'll learn

• Install Python and write your first programs
• Work with strings, numbers, lists, tuples and dictionaries
• Use conditionals, loops and functions
• Import modules and use the OS, file, CSV and datetime libraries
• Handle errors and write unit tests
• Manage packages with virtual environments and request web pages

## Requirements

• No programming experience required
• A computer running Windows, macOS or Linux
• A text editor or IDE

## Who this course is for

• Complete beginners to programming
• Students and analysts who want to automate tasks
• Developers new to Python

## Course details

**Instructor:** Corey Schafer
**Video source:** YouTube playlist "Python Programming Beginner Tutorials" by Corey Schafer
**Video language:** English, can be dubbed into many languages
**Content:** 26 lessons · about 8.9 hours

lessons.title: Install and Setup for Mac and Windows
lessons.description: In this Python Beginner Tutorial, we will start with the basics of how to install and setup Python for Mac and Windows. We will also take a look at the interactive prompt, as well as creating and running our first script. Let's get started.

lessons.title: Strings - Working with Textual Data
lessons.description: In this Python Beginner Tutorial, we will begin learning about the string data type. Strings allow us to work with textual data in Python. We will be going over different ways to format strings, and also a lot of useful string methods. Let's get started.

lessons.title: Integers and Floats - Working with Numeric Data
lessons.description: In this Python Beginner Tutorial, we will begin learning about integers and floats. Integers and Floats allow us to work with numeric data in Python. We will be learning how to perform basic arithmetic, as well as how to compare numeric values. Let's get started.

lessons.title: Lists, Tuples, and Sets
lessons.description: In this Python Beginner Tutorial, we will begin learning about Lists, Tuples, and Sets in Python. Lists and Tuples allow us to work with sequential data, and Sets allow us to work with unordered unique values.

lessons.title: Dictionaries - Working with Key-Value Pairs
lessons.description: In this Python Beginner Tutorial, we will begin learning about dictionaries. Dictionaries allow us to work with key-value pairs in Python. We will go over dictionary methods, how to add and remove values, and also how to loop through the key-value pairs. Let's get started.

lessons.title: Conditionals and Booleans - If, Else, and Elif Statements
lessons.description: In this Python Beginner Tutorial, we will begin learning about if, elif, and else conditionals in Python. We will also be learning about Booleans and what evaluates to True and False. Let's get started.

lessons.title: Loops and Iterations - For/While Loops
lessons.description: In this Python Beginner Tutorial, we will begin learning about Loops and Iterations. Specifically, we will be looking at the for/while loops. We will learn about iteration and also how to break out of the loops using the break and continue keywords. Let's get started.

lessons.title: Functions
lessons.description: In this Python Beginner Tutorial, we will begin learning how to write functions. Functions are one of the most important things to learn in Python Programming and will take us to the next level. We will learn how to create/define functions, how to pass in arguments, and also how to return values.

lessons.title: Import Modules and Exploring The Standard Library
lessons.description: In this Python Beginner Tutorial, we will begin learning how to import modules in Python. We will learn how to import modules we have written, as well as modules from the Standard Library. We will also explore sys.path and how imported modules are found. Let's get started.

lessons.title: OS Module - Use Underlying Operating System Functionality
lessons.description: In this Python Tutorial, we will be going over the 'os' module. The os module allows us to access functionality of the underlying operating system.

lessons.title: File Objects - Reading and Writing to Files
lessons.description: In this Python Tutorial, we will be learning how to read and write to files. You will likely come into contact with file objects at some point while using Python, so knowing how to read and write from them is extremely important.

lessons.title: How to Set the Path and Switch Between Different Versions/Executables (Windows)
lessons.description: In this Python Programming Tutorial, we will be learning how to set the PATH environment variable on the Windows Operating Systems.

lessons.title: How to Set the Path and Switch Between Different Versions/Executables (Mac & Linux)
lessons.description: In this Python Programming Tutorial, we will be learning how to set the PATH environment variable on the Mac & Linux Operating Systems.

lessons.title: Automate Parsing and Renaming of Multiple Files
lessons.description: In this video we will be writing a quick script to automate the parsing and renaming of multiple files. Writing quick scripts to automate boring and repetitive tasks is a great way to learn Python and it is a great way to save time. Let's get started.

lessons.title: CSV Module - How to Read, Parse, and Write CSV Files
lessons.description: In this Python Programming Tutorial, we will be learning how to work with csv files using the csv module. We will learn how to read, parse, and write to csv files. CSV stands for "Comma-Separated Values". It is a common format for storing information.

lessons.title: Real World Example - Parsing Names From a CSV to an HTML List
lessons.description: In this Python Programming Tutorial, we'll be learning how to parse a CSV file and output the data to an HTML unordered list. This is a real world problem I ran into with my website.

lessons.title: Datetime Module - How to work with Dates, Times, Timedeltas, and Timezones
lessons.description: In this Python Tutorial, we will be learning how to use the datetime module. The datetime module is important to understand, because you will be working with dates and times in just about every application you write.

lessons.title: Variable Scope - Understanding the LEGB rule and global/nonlocal statements
lessons.description: In this Python Tutorial, we will be going over variable scope in Python. Scope is important because we need to understand it in just about every program we write. It allows us to understand where our variables can be seen from within our program and also what values these variables hold.

lessons.title: Sorting Lists, Tuples, and Objects
lessons.description: In this video we will be learning how to sort lists, tuples, and other objects in Python. We will start by performing simple sorts on a list of integers and then move on to slightly more advanced sorting using custom criteria. Let's get started.

lessons.title: Using Try/Except Blocks for Error Handling
lessons.description: We've all run into errors and exceptions while writing Python programs. In this video, we will learn how we can handle exceptions in specific ways and also look at the control flow of a try/except/else/finally statement.

lessons.title: Unit Testing Your Code with the unittest Module
lessons.description: In this Python Programming Tutorial, we will be learning how to unit-test our code using the unittest module. Unit testing will allow you to be more comfortable with refactoring and knowing whether or not your updates broke any of your existing code.

lessons.title: Pipenv - Easily Manage Packages and Virtual Environments

Learn Node.js from the V8 engine and modules to servers, Express and a MongoDB-backed to-do app.

Node.js lets you run JavaScript on the server. This course starts with how Node works and builds up to creating servers, serving pages and using Express.

You will learn modules, events, file handling and streams, then template engines, middleware and forms, and finish with a to-do app connected to MongoDB.

## What you'll learn

• Understand how Node.js and the V8 engine work
• Use modules, events and the file system
• Create servers and work with streams and buffers
• Serve HTML and JSON and handle routing
• Build apps with Express, middleware and template engines
• Connect an application to MongoDB

## Requirements

• Basic JavaScript
• Node.js installed
• A code editor

• JavaScript developers moving to the back end

courses.title: PyTorch for Deep Learning: Beginner Course
courses.description:
Learn PyTorch from tensors and autograd to CNNs, RNNs and model deployment.

PyTorch is the leading framework for deep-learning research. This course teaches it step by step, starting with tensors and gradients and building up to complete training pipelines.

You will implement regression and classification, use datasets and data loaders, build feed-forward and convolutional networks, apply transfer learning and finish with RNNs and deployment.

## What you'll learn

• Install PyTorch and work with tensors
• Understand gradients, backpropagation and gradient descent
• Build a full training pipeline with models, losses and optimisers
• Use Dataset, DataLoader and transforms
• Build feed-forward and convolutional neural networks
• Apply transfer learning, RNNs and deploy a model

## Requirements

• Python programming
• Basic linear algebra and calculus
• A computer; a GPU is optional

• Python developers moving into deep learning

Each lesson then covers one layer of defence: identity, endpoints, networks, applications and data, ending with detection and response.
